stories.dek: Shares fell again, but the shape of the fall changed. The S&P 500 is down 0.45%, the Dow 0.64% and small companies 0.93% — the worst of the four. Two hours ago the tech-heavy Nasdaq was falling five and a half times as fast as the Dow; now they are falling at the same rate, so this is no longer just expensive tech being marked down. Oil is up 4.33% to $96.15, which feeds inflation, and government borrowing costs hit fresh highs for the day. Gold fell too, at $4,294.10 — in a real panic gold rises, so this is the cost of money going up, not fear. Watch the oil price into the US close.
stories.headline: Oil jumps over 4% and the sell-off spreads beyond tech shares
stories.short: Oil up 4%, and now everything is falling together

claims.claim: VIX level, change and prior close
Distance to the ladder's 30 buy window, calculated

stories.dek: The VIX, the market's fear gauge, is at 16.30, up 7.39% on the day from Wednesday's 15.18. The BuyTrigger ladder reads under 15 as calm, 15 to 20 as normal, 20 to 30 as nervous and above 30 as the system's buy window. So a gauge that has risen three days running is still only in the normal band, and it sits 13.70 points below the level where the system starts treating a fall as an opportunity. For anyone holding good businesses for years, that is the useful point: a broad down day is not automatically a cheap day. Watch whether 20 gets touched into the close.
stories.headline: The fear gauge climbs to 16.3 but stays in its normal range
stories.short: Fear gauge at 16.3 — still normal, not a buy window

stories.dek: Oracle has sent a force majeure notice to Blue Owl Capital over Project Jupiter, its New Mexico data centre, which would let Oracle delay payments if the site does not open on time in 2028. Publicly the company says "Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule." About $18bn of debt was raised against the campus and was already trading at distressed prices. Oracle shares fell 4.18% to $138.52, touching $133.48 — 7.7% below Wednesday's close. Blue Owl, the lender, fell 4.12%, almost exactly as much. For long-term holders this is the AI build-out question made concrete: not whether the data centres get built, but who carries the cost if they are late. Watch for an Oracle filing.
stories.headline: Oracle moves to delay data centre payments it says are on schedule
stories.short: Oracle sends legal notice on data centre, shares drop 4%

Robinhood fall since the 14:34 UK opening read of $122.16, calculated
Bitcoin price, exchange ticker with its own timestamp
Bitcoin rise since the 14:34 UK read of $84,066.85, calculated

stories.dek: Robinhood is down 1.83% at $120.45, having fallen a further 1.40% since the US market opened — while Bitcoin went the other way, up 0.29% to $84,309.87. That matters because for the past two days Robinhood had moved almost step for step with Bitcoin, up and down, and that explanation has now stopped working. When a reliable relationship breaks, the honest position is that today's fall needs a different reason, and no company news has surfaced to supply one. For a long-term holder it is a reminder that a share can be sold for reasons that have nothing to do with the business. Watch whether the Bitcoin link resumes by the close.
stories.headline: Robinhood falls while Bitcoin rises, breaking its usual pattern
stories.short: Robinhood down 1.8% even as Bitcoin ticks up

Change from July, with margin of error as printed
Change from a year earlier, with margin of error as printed
Months' supply of unsold new homes
Median sales price and year-on-year change

stories.dek: The Census Bureau reported August sales of new homes running at 684,000 a year, described as 6.4% above July. In the same sentence it prints a margin of error of plus or minus 19.5% — three times the size of the move — so statistically the direction is not established. Two figures are solid: there are 8.5 months of unsold homes at the current sales pace, and the typical new home sold for $393,700, down 5.8% on a year ago. That is what a 5.11% government borrowing rate does to the most rate-sensitive corner of the economy, and it sits awkwardly against Wednesday's survey showing the fastest business growth in five years.
stories.headline: New home sales look up 6%, but the error margin is larger
stories.short: New home sales: the 6% rise proves nothing

claims.claim: Nvidia share price and change

stories.dek: Asked about artificial intelligence ahead of his meeting with China's Xi Jinping, President Trump said he wants to "leave it exactly where it is" — meaning no loosening of the rules that limit which advanced chips can be sold to China. Nvidia shares are down 1.46% at $222.22. Investors had treated an easing of those restrictions as a possible upside surprise from this week's summit, so its absence removes a hoped-for catalyst rather than creating a new problem. For a long-term holder the business case for Nvidia rests on Western data centre demand, which this does not touch. The summit continues on Friday.
stories.headline: Trump says chip export rules stay put, giving Nvidia nothing new
stories.short: Trump on AI rules: leave it exactly where it is

claims.claim: Micron share price and change
Recovery from the 14:34 UK opening read of $1,047.43, calculated
Fiscal fourth-quarter results date

stories.dek: Micron, the memory-chip maker, is down 1.32% at $1,057.71 — but that is a recovery of 0.98% from where it stood when the US market opened, and it is no longer the weakest name in the AI supply chain. It had been the worst of the group for three straight editions as rising interest rates hit the most expensive shares hardest. The company reports its fourth-quarter results on 30 September, confirmed on Micron's own investor site, and will do so with that discount already applied to the share price. For a long-term holder the question is whether the results justify the multiple, not whether the shares bounced this afternoon.
stories.headline: Micron recovers off the day's low with results due next week
stories.short: Micron claws back, no longer the worst in the chain
